chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not appropriate for anyone to take from the soil surrounding the House (Kaaba), and if he takes something of that, he should return it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking soil from the Kaaba in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the status of the Kaaba's soil, ruling that it is not proper for individuals to appropriate it for personal keepsakes. The instruction to return any taken soil underscores the principle of *isti'ab* (presumption of ownership) being limited, ensuring the sanctity of the Sacred House remains distinct from private possession. This ruling is often cited in discussions regarding the permissibility of taking blessed earth (*turab*) from holy sites for veneration or healing.
